observations: Figure 2 shows four panels (A–D) depicting decomposition of productivity effects, industry shifts, direct displacement effects, and ripple effects on hourly wage (log scale, 2020 dollars) for demographic groups by education level (Less than high school, High school, Some college, College, Postgraduate).
Each panel contains colored scatter-like clusters where marker sizes are proportional to the average 2018–2022 employment level of each group; colors indicate education level.
The horizontal axis is 'Hourly wage in 2018-2022 (log scale, 2020 dollars)' ranging from ~2.5 to 4.5.
The vertical axis ranges from -0.15 to +0.15, representing estimated wage effects.
Panel C: Adding direct task displacement.

Notes state the figure is based on estimates of the propagation matrix from Acemoglu and Restrepo (2022), combined with exposure to easy/hard AI tasks; final panel incorporates direct displacement and ripple effects.

Text below figure discusses row 7 (GDP impact estimate), assuming capital stock adjustment within 10 years and constant required rate of return; yields upper bound GDP impact of 1.4% (or 1.56% when easy/hard distinction not drawn); capital share increases by ~0.31 percentage points.
uncertainties: Marker sizes are proportional to average 2018–2022 employment level but exact values are not numerically reported in the figure.
Exact coordinates of data points are not provided—only visual clusters are shown.
The text states 'See text for details' regarding color coding and marker sizing, implying missing quantitative detail in the figure itself.

Required rate of return on capital investments is assumed constant, though a 'sizable investment' may cause it to increase.
